programmes.d: We’re spelling tonight! Walter Matthau and Johnny quiz one another on difficult words. Matthau recalls filming Tunisia and shows a clip from his movie, Pirates.
The king of stand up, Richard Pryor discusses his recent trip to Zimbabwe and daily life since quitting drugs and alcohol.
A 12-year-old Fred Savage "Kind-Of-Sorta" has a girlfriend, plus future host Jay Leno stops by and Brian Gillis does magic
Newly slender super-comic Richard Pryor discusses dropping 20 pounds for a movie role and driving his Ferrari across the US. Madonna spouse Sean Pean chats about life with the Material Girl.

programmes.t: The Best of the Carol Burnett Show
programmes.d: Sketches include Vincent crossing paths with Alice Portnoy and understudying for Ham Actor Harvey, then saying 'goodnight, Joan Boy' in 'The Walnuts.'
John Candy stops by with screen icon Maureen O'Hara. Plus, Jim Valvano appears and Johnny gives up smoking in the monologue.
Jonathan Winters crashes Carol's Q&A, while the legendary "Professor" Sid Caesar teaches Carol self-defense, then joins the gang for a spoof of Ancient Rome movies. "Hail Caesar," indeed!
The delightful Dick Van Dyke is Carol's guest, lending his impressive talents to an homage to Shirley Temple films, "Little Miss Showbiz", with Carol as bratty orphan Honey Bunny.
Another superstar panel, with Lynn Redgrave and Tom Hanks, who talks about learning to juggle.
Ed Sullivan presents performances by Diana Ross & The Supremes, Dusty Springfield, Gladys Knight & The Pips, Janis Joplin, and The Supremes.
Carol's guests tonight are Burt Reynolds and Nanette Fabray, who join the gang for a series of Carol's patented commercial parodies, and the late night adventure movie "The Lavender Pimpernel."
Albert Brooks and Susan Sarandon head to the couch for conversation topics ranging from how to know when you're in love to clam shucking.

programmes.t: The Best of The Ed Sullivan Show
programmes.d: Ed Sullivan presents Janis Joplin, Honey LTD, Les Samurai, Ed Ames, The Carals, Buddy Hackett, Chet Atkins, Floyd Cramer, and Boots Randolph.
Pat Carroll and Jack Jones are Carol's exciting and new guests. Pat and Carol play competing commercial actresses up for the same role. Plus: another chapter of "As The Stomach Turns."
The bikini’d star of Laugh-in and Oscar winner Goldie Hawn talks about giving birth. And what’s the big deal with King Tut? Buck Henry, who created Get Smart and wrote The Graduate has some thoughts.
Frankly my dear, guest star Richard Chamberlain gives it his all in "Gone With The Breeze". And in the latest "Carol & Sis" sketch, it's one sibling too many when Roger's big sister Mimi shows up.
Columbo Star Peter Falk discusses the series’ ties to the Mensa Society. Heavyweight champion and civil rights activist Muhammad Ali shows a clip from The Greatest.

programmes.t: The Best of The Ed Sullivan Show
programmes.d: Ed Sullivan presents B.J. Thomas, Lou Rawls, The Canestrellis, Robert Klein, Roberta Peters, Robert Merrill, The Jovers, Little Anthony and The Imperials.
TV comedy icon Bob Newhart stops by, along with Saundra Santiago and Teresa Ganzel.
Delightful Imogene Coca joins Carol to play friends enlisted to appear in a coffee commercial, while Harvey and Carol shine in an interview with Miss America and the parody "Bonnie And Clod."
Ken Berry and Nanette Fabray join in tonight's episode, which includes Carol as a dowdy secretary discouraging some glamorous temp applicants, and the movie spoof "Flight 13 To Nowhere."
Even Buddy Hackett bombs sometimes--just not for Johnny Carson. Rocky Graziano stops by and Johnny wonders if $2,000-worth of ornaments on a Christmas tree is too much.

programmes.t: The Best of the Carol Burnett Show
programmes.d: Jack Klugman is tonight's guest star! Jack plays a skeptical man annoyed by his sister-in-law's visiting date--a clairvoyant.
Albert Brooks talks puppy love, Susan Sarandon talks clam shucking and Carnac the Magnificent works his magic.
No holiday is safe: Halloween, Thanksgiving, and Easter all get the Carlin stand-up treatment in this episode also featuring Keshia Knight Pulliam.
Rock Hudson is tonight's guest star, appearing with Carol as husband and wife news anchors, and as secretary Mrs. Wiggins' lunch date, who's utterly smitten with her.
Superstar comic Jerry Seinfeld skewers Rambo flicks. Arnold Schwarzenegger plays a Russian cop and learns the language! Tennis great Andre Agassi recalls hitting balls with Jimmy Connors.
Carol welcomes Valerie Harper and Tim Conway as her guests! Valerie joins Carol on a blind double date, Tim is the world's oldest fireman, and ham actor Harvey newest co-star is a miscast Charo type.
The brilliant Richard Pryor describes his transforming time in Zimbabwe and quitting drugs and booze. Hollywood legend and non-singer Bette Davis talks about her new record!
James Garner shares the gruesome details of his recent bypass surgery and thanks well-wishers for the 9,000 get-well cards he received. The operation has not, thankfully, hurt his golf game.

programmes.t: The Best of The Ed Sullivan Show
programmes.d: Ed Sullivan presents Stevie Wonder, The Brooklyn Bridge, The Jovers, Jane Morgan, Anna Maria Alberghetti, and Norm Crosby.
Carol's guests are George Chakiris and Shirley Jones! Chakiris joins Carol for the Q&A, while the latest "Carol & Sis" sketch finds Jones playing Roger's temp secretary--much to Carol's dismay.
Tonight's guests are Helen Reddy and John Byner, who appear in a series of commercial parodies. John also takes part in a "Nora Desmond" sketch, while Vicki plays gossip columnist "Rona Rumor."
